title: The Counting Blindness
question: Volunteers counting basketball passes famously miss a person in a gorilla suit strolling through the game. What walks past focused counters unseen?
correctExplanation: The gorilla — focused counting burns the attention needed to notice it. Looking never equals seeing.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is the gorilla. Pass-counting consumes the attentional budget entirely; an obvious intruder crosses unseen. Sustained focus blinds peripheries absolutely.
lessonContent:
Sustained focus blinds peripheries absolutely.
Counting consumes whole attentional budgets.
Looking never equals seeing anything.
Obvious intruders cross unseen routinely.
Share this: count passes and miss everything.

title: The Door Swap
question: A stranger asking directions is briefly blocked by a carried door — and a different person continues the conversation. Most pedestrians never notice. What escapes them?
correctExplanation: The switch — change blindness: visual details of strangers never encode. Conversations continue with replacements unnoticed.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is the switch. Door-study pedestrians fail to detect a changed interlocutor because faces of strangers encode thinly. Memory stores gist, never mugshots.
lessonContent:
Stranger faces encode thinly at best.
Gist memory skips identifying details.
Doors swap people unnoticed daily.
Conversations continue past substitutions.
Share this: describe one stranger precisely.

title: The Jam Defense
question: Shoppers choosing jams are secretly handed their rejected jar — then fluently justify preferring it. What manipulation goes undetected?
correctExplanation: The swap — choice blindness: decisions unmonitored, justifications improvised. Preferences narrated after the fact.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is the swap. Johansson's shoppers defend jams they rejected seconds earlier: choice monitoring is theater, confabulation the understudy. Reasons follow choices, rarely lead.
lessonContent:
Reasons follow choices more than lead.
Confabulation understudies every decision.
Monitoring is theater; narrative improvises.
Defended picks may never have been picked.
Share this: defend one unchosen jam.

title: The Expert Blindness
question: Expert radiologists hunting nodules miss a drawn gorilla on CT scans; novice counters miss costumed intruders. What single phenomenon covers both failures?
correctExplanation: Inattentional blindness — expertise upgrades targets, never attention itself. Focused tasks blind all ranks equally.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is inattentional blindness. Nodule-hunters and pass-counters share one bottleneck: attended tasks consume seeing. Expertise changes what, never whether, focus blinds.
lessonContent:
Expertise upgrades targets, never attention.
Bottlenecks blind all ranks equally.
Focused tasks consume seeing itself.
What-focus differs; blindness persists.
Share this: miss one obvious gorilla.

title: The Name Beacon
question: Shadowing speech in one ear, listeners ignore the other channel entirely — except for one stimulus that always breaks through. What pierces the block?
correctExplanation: One's own name — the cocktail-party beacon: self-relevance pierces inattention automatically. Identity monitors all channels at once.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is one's own name. Cherry's shadowers miss language switches yet catch their names: a background watchman screens everything for self. Attention has a permanent back door.
lessonContent:
Identity monitors all channels at once.
Self-relevance pierces every block automatically.
Background watchmen screen for selfhood.
Names are permanent back doors.
Share this: whisper one name across noise.

title: The Fading Watch
question: Radar operators miss steadily more signals as shifts drag on — attention itself tires like a muscle. What fades with time on task?
correctExplanation: Vigilance — sustained attention decrements measurably within half an hour. Watches tire faster than eyes.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is vigilance. Mackworth's clock-watchers proved attention fades as a function of time alone: signals missed multiply across shifts. Muscles tire; so does monitoring.
lessonContent:
Monitoring tires like muscles do.
Signals missed multiply across shifts.
Time-on-task degrades detection steadily.
Watches need relief, never willpower.
Share this: relieve one watch early.

title: The Wandering Half
question: Experience-sampling finds minds stray from the present task nearly half of waking life. What occupies this enormous share?
correctExplanation: Mind-wandering — nearly half of consciousness runs off-task: planning, replaying, imagining. Presence is the minority report.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is mind-wandering. Killingsworth's pings caught stray thought around 47% of hours: humans live largely elsewhere. Unhappiness tracks wandering, not location.
lessonContent:
Presence is consciousness's minority report.
Stray thought fills nearly half of hours.
Wandering predicts unhappiness better than location.
Elsewhere is the default address.
Share this: catch one wandering episode.

title: The Skipped Banner
question: Web users automatically skip page regions shaped like advertisements — regardless of actual content placed there. What gets ignored by shape alone?
correctExplanation: Banner areas — shape-learned skipping: ad-geometry means do-not-read. Content dies at the border of learned blindness.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is banner areas. Eye-tracking shows learned avoidance of ad-shaped zones whatever they hold. Geometry triggers skipping before content loads.
lessonContent:
Geometries trigger skipping pre-content.
Learned avoidance outruns reading entirely.
Shapes mean do-not-read reliably.
Borders kill content before loading.
Share this: read one banner-shaped box.

title: The Threshold Forgetting
question: Walking through doorways measurably impairs recall of intentions formed in the previous room. What does crossing thresholds disrupt?
correctExplanation: Doorway effect — event boundaries flush working memory: new rooms, new files. Intentions die at thresholds routinely.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is doorway effect. Radvansky's walkers forget errands upon room change: boundaries segment experience and dump buffers. Architecture edits memory silently.
lessonContent:
Boundaries segment experience silently.
New rooms open new mental files.
Buffers dump at every threshold.
Architecture edits memory constantly.
Share this: blame one doorway aloud.

title: The Hands-Free Myth
question: Hands-free phone calls impair driving about as badly as drunk driving. With hands free and eyes forward, what stays impaired?
correctExplanation: Driver attention — conversation consumes the mind, not the hands. Eyes forward, mind elsewhere: inattention blindness at speed.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is driver attention. Strayer's simulators prove hands-free parity with intoxication: cognitive load, not manual load, kills. Forward eyes never guarantee present minds.
lessonContent:
Cognitive load kills regardless of hands.
Forward eyes hide absent minds.
Conversation consumes driving attention.
Hands-free never means brain-free.
Share this: hang up before driving once.

title: The Fountain Walker
question: Phone-distracted pedestrians walk into fountains, poles, and traffic with rising injury counts. What modern hazard has a diagnosis?
correctExplanation: Distracted walking — screens capture gaze while streets demand it. Fountains fill with the inattentive annually.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is distracted walking. Emergency rooms code the collisions: eyes down, world unmonitored. Urban furniture defeats divided pedestrians reliably.
lessonContent:
Screens capture gaze streets demand.
Divided pedestrians lose to furniture.
Down-eyes forfeit right-of-way awareness.
Fountains collect the inattentive yearly.
Share this: pocket one phone per block.

title: The Gun Memory
question: Robbery witnesses recall the weapon vividly but the face barely at all. What steals face memory during crimes?
correctExplanation: Weapon focus — threat captures the attentional bottleneck, starving face encoding. Guns photograph; faces blur.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is weapon focus. Eyes lock threat while faces pass unencoded: attention is zero-sum under fear. Testimony remembers steel, forgets features.
lessonContent:
Threats monopolize encoding bandwidth.
Zero-sum attention starves faces for guns.
Fear photographs weapons, blurs people.
Bottlenecks pick threats over identities.
Share this: notice one face fully today.

title: The Tired Monitor
question: CCTV operators watching wall-to-wall screens miss incidents that later footage shows plainly. What fatigues across multi-screen shifts?
correctExplanation: Monitoring fatigue — sustained divided watching degrades exactly like radar duty. Walls of screens exhaust faster than single views.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is monitoring fatigue. More screens multiply load, not coverage: attention thins across displays until incidents pass unseen. Coverage promised exceeds attention delivered.
lessonContent:
More screens multiply load, not coverage.
Divided watching thins to transparency.
Promised coverage exceeds delivered attention.
Walls exhaust faster than windows.
Share this: watch one screen truly.

title: The Stubborn Word
question: Naming ink colors while ignoring the color words themselves (RED in blue ink) slows everyone measurably. What captures attention against orders?
correctExplanation: Stroop interference — reading runs automatically and collides with color-naming. Literacy hijacks intention effortlessly.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is Stroop interference. Word meanings barge in uninvited: suppressing reading costs time every trial. Automaticity overrules orders reliably.
lessonContent:
Automaticity overrules orders reliably.
Reading barges in uninvited always.
Suppression costs time every trial.
Literacy hijacks color intentions.
Share this: fail one Stroop test proudly.

title: The Blink Gap
question: In rapid image streams, viewers spotting a first target miss a second landing a fraction of a second later. What blanks the follow-up?
correctExplanation: Attentional blink — processing the first target occupies the bottleneck for ~half a second. Seconds in streams vanish during encoding.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is attentional blink. RSVP experiments prove encoding blocks follow-ups for hundreds of milliseconds: attention blinks after each catch. Streams outrun bottlenecks routinely.
lessonContent:
Encoding blocks follow-ups briefly always.
Bottlenecks blink after every catch.
Streams outrun capacity routinely.
Half-seconds swallow whole targets.
Share this: blink through one stream.

title: The Misdirected Eye
question: Stage magicians make audiences miss blatant methods by choreographing gaze and timing. What do they weaponize?
correctExplanation: Misdirected attention — gaze choreographed toward decoys while method happens off-look. Magic is applied inattention science.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is misdirected attention. Macknik's magicians prove social cues steer seeing: look where pointed, miss what matters. Wonder is engineered blindness.
lessonContent:
Wonder is engineered blindness precisely.
Social cues steer seeing reliably.
Decoys choreograph gaze away methodically.
Magic applies inattention science nightly.
Share this: watch magician's hands only.

title: The Soldier's Shield
question: Mindfulness training protected soldiers' working memory through brutal predeployment stress where controls declined. What buffered their minds?
correctExplanation: Mindfulness training — Jha's troops held working memory steady through stress that sank controls. Practice shields cognition measurably.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is mindfulness training. Eight weeks buffered brains against predeployment erosion: attention trained like muscle resists stress atrophy. Shields are built, never issued.
lessonContent:
Practice shields cognition measurably.
Stress erodes untrained minds first.
Muscles of attention resist atrophy.
Shields built beat armor issued.
Share this: train attention ten minutes.

title: The Park Prescription
question: Walks in nature restore depleted directed attention significantly better than equal city walks. What heals tired focus?
correctExplanation: Nature exposure — Kaplan's restoration theory: soft fascination rests directed attention while cities tax it. Parks prescribe focus.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is nature exposure. Controlled comparisons favor green over gray for attention recovery: effortless fascination restores effortful focus. Prescriptions grow on trees.
lessonContent:
Soft fascination rests directed focus.
Cities tax what parks restore.
Effortless attention heals effortful kinds.
Prescriptions grow on trees literally.
Share this: dose one green hour.

title: The Waking Blackout
question: After sleepless nights, attention blanks for seconds at a time while eyes stay open. What interrupts wakefulness in micro-gaps?
correctExplanation: Microsleeps — 1-to-10-second neural blackouts with eyes open. Wakefulness strobes before it fails outright.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is microsleeps. PVT tests catch attention winking out in seconds-long gaps: open eyes, offline brain. Strobing precedes shutdown reliably.
lessonContent:
Wakefulness strobes before failing outright.
Open eyes hide offline brains.
Seconds-long gaps riddle tired attention.
Blackouts precede shutdowns reliably.
Share this: nap before one long drive.

title: The Caffeine Limit
question: Caffeine reliably restores alertness after sleep loss — but leaves complex reasoning impaired. What does the drug actually fix?
correctExplanation: Alertness alone — caffeine masks sleep pressure without restoring cognition. Awake is not the same as able.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is alertness alone. Drake's studies split the effects: vigilance rebounds, judgment stays impaired. Coffee borrows wakefulness it cannot spend on thought.
lessonContent:
Wakefulness differs from ability entirely.
Masks hide pressure; they never pay debts.
Vigilance rebounds while judgment lags.
Borrowed alertness spends poorly on thought.
Share this: doubt one coffee miracle.

title: The Drunken Spotlight
question: Intoxicated people fixate on the loudest cue in the room while missing everything subtle. What narrows attention with drink?
correctExplanation: Alcohol myopia — Steele's theory: drink shrinks attentional breadth to the salient. Spotlights replace floodlights reliably.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is alcohol myopia. Salience monopolizes narrowed fields: loudest cues win unopposed while context vanishes. Myopia explains barroom tunnel vision exactly.
lessonContent:
Salience monopolizes narrowed fields fully.
Spotlights replace floodlights under drink.
Context vanishes first, cues remain.
Myopia explains tunnel vision exactly.
Share this: widen one narrowed field.

title: The Threat Tunnel
question: Anxiety shrinks attentional breadth toward threats, starving peripheral awareness. What does dread do to the spotlight?
correctExplanation: Threat narrowing — dread focuses on danger and blinds surroundings. Tunnel vision is anxiety's optics.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is threat narrowing. Attentional control theory: worry consumes the breadth peripheral awareness needs. Spotlights tighten as threats loom.
lessonContent:
Dread tightens spotlights automatically.
Breadth starves while threats feast.
Tunnel vision is anxiety's optics.
Worry consumes peripheral awareness.
Share this: widen one dreaded view.

title: The Looping Sorrow
question: Depressive rumination chews the same thoughts endlessly, occupying the working memory daily life needs. What drains cognition in depression?
correctExplanation: Rumination — looping sorrow occupies bandwidth grief needs for living. Thought chews cud instead of moving.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is rumination. Working memory filled with replay leaves none for now: cognition starves amid plenty. Loops consume what living requires.
lessonContent:
Loops consume what living requires.
Replay starves present-tense bandwidth.
Chewing cud never nourishes action.
Bandwidth filled cannot serve now.
Share this: break one loop kindly.

title: The Power Blindness
question: The socially powerful systematically neglect others' perspectives — interrupting more, listening less, modeling minds poorly. What does power impair?
correctExplanation: Perspective-taking — power reduces other-modeling: the mighty navigate people as obstacles. Thrones narrow theory of mind.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is perspective-taking. Galinsky's experiments show power priming cuts perspective accuracy: interruptions rise, listening falls. Altitude blinds to other minds reliably.
lessonContent:
Altitude blinds to other minds reliably.
Thrones narrow theory of mind steadily.
Interruptions rise as listening falls.
Power unchecks self-focus automatically.
Share this: model one other mind fully.

title: The Scarcity Levy
question: Poverty measurably depletes mental bandwidth — the poor decide worse with money partly because money worries consume cognition. What does scarcity charge?
correctExplanation: A bandwidth tax — Mullainathan's scarcity work: worry levies IQ points directly. Poverty taxes minds, not just wallets.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is a bandwidth tax. Sugarcane farmers score worse pre-harvest (poor) than post-harvest (paid): same brains, taxed bandwidth. Scarcity levies cognition itself.
lessonContent:
Worry levies IQ points directly.
Same brains, taxed bandwidth differ.
Poverty charges minds, never just wallets.
Scarcity is a cognitive condition too.
Share this: lift one bandwidth tax.
